answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to lock a small refundable stake behind a cipher-based identity key, so spawning thousands of fake agents gets expensive fast. Reputation then grows like a trellis: peers only vouch for agents whose past work they actually verified, and trust spreads along those attested links instead of from self-declared claims. Like cedar that takes years to mature, an identity gains weight only through sustained useful service, so a sybil swarm that appears overnight stays light and untrusted while genuine agents accumulate real history.
